changelog.change: Added the Time Trial screen's wording: the start card, the countdown's accessible name, the time-up screen, and the best-run line.
changelog.why: Row 23 - the Time Trial ships, and the clock is the one piece of chrome in this game that a player must understand before they touch anything, so every word around it is copy rather than a string inside a component. time-trial-remaining is the countdown's ACCESSIBLE NAME: the digits carry the value, and without a name beside them a screen-reader user would hear a bare number counting down with nothing saying what it counts. The start screen exists because a clock that begins while the first board is still arriving would charge a player for the network, so the run opens on a card that says how long the sprint is and waits to be tapped - and that card needs a sentence of its own. time-trial-new-best is deliberately separate from time-trial-best: a record that was just broken and a record that stands are different pieces of news, and showing the same line for both would make beating your own score silent.

changelog.change: Added the Infinite screen's wording: the difficulty chooser and its three bands, the next-puzzle control, the run counter, and the unavailable screen.
changelog.why: Row 22 - the Infinite Mode ships, and the difficulty names are the first time this game has ever shown a player the word easy, medium or hard. They are copy rather than identifiers for exactly that reason: the band slug is what travels in a baked pool item and what the generator registry speaks, and a Tamil label baked beside it could only be corrected by a rebuild. They double as the accessible name of the chooser's three buttons, so a screen-reader user hears the band rather than a bare position. The run counter is the only new number on the screen and it is deliberately a count of what this sitting has solved rather than a score: an endless mode has no end to score against, and the honest thing to show is how far the player has come.

changelog.change: Added the Journey screen's wording: the map label, the three node states, the progress line, the back-to-map control, and the unavailable screen.
changelog.why: Row 17 - the Journey Mode ships, and every sentence on it is a sentence a player reads. The three state words carry more weight here than anywhere else in the app: they are the ACCESSIBLE NAME of a node, so a screen-reader user hears 'three, word search, locked' where a sighted one sees a dashed circle, and without them the map would announce a bare number and mean nothing. The Journey's own TITLE is deliberately NOT here - it arrives with the path, because a copy map that needed an entry minted for every file dropped would be exactly the redeploy the data-defined path exists to avoid. The node-state slugs are named for the states themselves rather than for this one path, so a second Journey needs no new copy at all.

changelog.change: Added the word-ladder Game name and the result card's stat and share wording.
changelog.why: Row 16 - the sixth Game reaches players, so the session rail needs a Tamil word for the board it is naming; without it the rail would have printed the raw slug. The other six strings are the completion moment: a climber who finishes is shown TIME, INSTINCT, RETRIES and STREAK and offered a card to copy, and every one of those is a sentence a player reads, so it lives here rather than inside the component. The streak label is deliberately NOT a new slug - the card reuses summary-streak, because a run named two different things on two screens reads as two different runs.

changelog.change: Added a Tamil name for each of the five Games, and the themed-round label.
changelog.why: A Daily day now holds three DIFFERENT Games, and until this the shell named none of them: a player finished a scramble and the next screen was a grid with no word for what it was. Five Games in one session must not read as five apps, so the session rail names the board the player is on - one Tamil word, in the same slot every time, changing as the day moves. The themed label is the other half of the same gap: the generator has dropped the category rung from every themed day since Row 15 on the stated grounds that 'the theme is already announced free in the round header', and no header announced it, so a themed day silently gave up a hint rung and returned nothing for it. The Game names are copy rather than identifiers - the gameId is what travels in the baked day - so they live here, and a slug with no entry renders its own slug rather than a blank.

Row 14 - an arrangement that is a real served word but not today's answer gets its own sentence, and a sentence a player reads is copy. It reaches the Game through the Mode's config slice, never an import, so the Game still sees nothing but its payload and context.

Row 15 - a themed day bakes the theme's SLUG, and the Tamil a player reads for it lives here. A category name is player-facing copy, so it is never baked into a dataset where correcting it would need a rebuild.

changelog.change: Added the Home, Daily, and end-of-session strings.
changelog.why: Row 13 - the first player-facing screens; every string a player reads lives here, never inside a component.
Row 7 - player-facing text keyed by stable slug, separate from app-config identifiers; entries land as UI rows add labels.
